title: 没有…那么: not as … as
summary: Lets you say one thing is not as good, big or fast as another, as in 我没有他那么高.
structure: A + 没有 + B + (那么 / 这么) + Adjective
explanation:
A 没有 B (那么) + adjective means 'A is not as … as B': 我没有他那么高 'I'm not as tall as him.' 那么 ('that') is optional but very common; use 这么 when B is right here.

This is the usual negative of a 比 sentence: 他比我高 → 我没有他高. Saying 不比 is possible but has a different, argumentative feel.

examples.en: I'm not as tall as him.
Today isn't as cold as yesterday.

examples.zh: 坐公交车没有坐地铁快。
examples.en: Taking the bus isn't as fast as the subway.

examples.zh: 我的汉语没有你这么好。
examples.en: My Chinese isn't as good as yours.

examples.zh: 这个饭馆没有那个饭馆贵。
examples.en: This restaurant isn't as expensive as that one.

mistakes.why: Use 那么, not 很, in this pattern.
The pattern uses 没有; 有 never takes 不.

exercises.en: Yesterday wasn't as hot as today.
why: Correct: A 没有 B 那么 + adjective.
不是 doesn't compare like this.
比 would say yesterday was hotter.

exercises.instruction: Turn it around: 'I'm not as tall as him.'
why: Correct: A 没有 B + adjective.
不比 has a different meaning, and 很 doesn't fit.
Use 那么 or nothing, not 很.

exercises.en: My room isn't as big as yours.
exercises.why: A + 没有 + B + 那么 + adjective.

why: Correct: this follows the pattern exactly.
没有 goes before B (他), not before the verb.

exercises.en: My Chinese isn't as good as yours (here).
why: Correct: 这么 / 那么 = so, as.
非常 doesn't fit this pattern.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'The subway isn't as cheap as the bus'?
why: Correct: A (地铁) 没有 B (公交车) 便宜.
This says the bus isn't as cheap.
This says the subway is cheaper.
